short: The Den read and write: the den Queries, the write use case and its gate, and Zurfur's two Atta hosts
is: The den module: the `Den` namespace's two Query use cases (`root`, `node`) that turn a driver's path pieces into Atta segments and call Atta's resolver; Zurfur's type enum (`DenType`) with its per-type kind and content-not-shown facts; `DenThing`, the Account or commission an open node stands for; `DenHost`, the read implementation of `atta::Host`, which records every node it answers for, admits from that record alone, and dispatches each folder through one exhaustive match to the arm of the team that owns it (den's own top level and posts here; identity's and commission's arms in their own modules' `den.rs`). The write: `Den::write` (crate-private), every typed write's one door, which checks the pool's verdict, opens one unit, makes the grant from the locked standing and builds Atta's act from it; and `DenWriteHost`, the second `atta::Host`, which serves no read and applies each checked act through the gate, which lends each act's handler a narrow, latched view and builds the act's entry itself. Commission create and rename are its real acts. Atta's types are imported only here; every public signature uses the application's own values.
conventions: Atta is imported only inside `src/den*`. The team arms (`user/den.rs`, `account/den.rs`, `character/den.rs`, `commission/den.rs`, `account/workflow/den.rs`) name Atta's values through `crate::den`'s re-exports.
Every miss is the one `DenError::NotFound`; the only other answer is `DenError::Store`. No arm, helper or Query panics, unwraps or expects; an impossible conversion makes the node absent.
A folder's real children and mounts are answered by the arm that owns the folder's place (`Place`); den's host matches over `Place` exhaustively, with no `_` arm.
`include_deleted` lives only in the host; Atta never sees it. The viewer comes from the session only, and every host method fails closed for any other viewer.
`admit` answers from the request's record alone: no store call, no failure.

The host keeps an arm's answer only when its place is a child of the folder's recorded place (`Place::is_child_of`) and, for `child`, its key is the key asked for; anything else is dropped unrecorded.

A place whose type doesn't show its content is closed: `child`, `children` and `mounts` below it answer nothing, so a listing and a typed path can't disagree. `/` and the top-level directories are traverse-only and list nothing. `/user/<did>` is looked up only for the session's own DID.

An open node's thing comes from the host's record for its real path, the recorded `Place` (`Place::thing`), in the same lookup as its soft-deleted word: no path segment is parsed for it, a mount carries its target's, and a card carries none.

The gate (`gate.rs`) is the only writer of node rows, the only issuer of a write capability and the only builder of a write's changelog entry: its free fn `gate` holds the crate's one `UnitOfWork::nodes()` call and `issue` the workspace's one `WriteCapability::gate_issued` call, each on its own `let` under its own `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`. `issue` is called only in `lend_as`; `lend_as` only in `lend` (once per leaf act, counted over `CommissionAct`'s production variants); and `RoleTable` is named, so implemented, only in `gate.rs`. `DenWriteHost::new` is named only in `write.rs`'s `written`, and `gate` only in `DenWriteHost::apply`. `tests/node_and_name_seams.rs` and `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` hold each of these.

A write is one unit: the node rows, the handler's write through its lent view and the gate's changelog entry land together or not at all. A refusal of any kind (Atta's, the gate's `DenRefusal`, a handler's) rides typed inside `Applied` and comes back as an `Err`, so the unit rolls back; a store failure is a `HostError`.
`Den::write`, its `Command` and `DenAct` stay crate-private (`write_gate_seams.rs` holds it): a driver reaches a write only through a typed use case that hands its act over and holds no unit.

An act's handler implements the gate's `Handler` (its `Role` marker, its `ENTRY` rule, `handle`); its needed role is read from the marker's `RoleTable::NEEDS` through `needs::<H>()`, never written apart, and a thing anchor whose act needs no role fails closed. The handler is lent `&mut Lent<'_, H::Role>`, a gate-owned view with private fields whose whole surface is `create` (on a creator's view only: the gate's node, the grant's actor and the gate's time, the handler choosing only `NewCommission`) and `lent` (the capability's commission, read after the act's writes); every method passes its own inner call through the latch, and a tripped latch fails the act whatever the handler answers. `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` pins the surface and the latch over every item of `gate.rs`, inline modules included, and holds that nothing else there reaches the private fields of `Lent` or `View`: no module but `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` (a module there is a descendant and sees them), no `.view` or `.repo` outside an `impl View` or `impl Lent`, and no struct literal or pattern of either but in `lend_as`, which builds both. The handler sees no unit, no changelog and no other repo method, and drafts no entry: the gate writes one entry through the rule's domain constructor (`NewChangelogEntry::created`, `NewChangelogEntry::renamed`), `Always` on every landing or `OnChange` only when the act changed a row (a rename to the stored name changes none), and refuses as a broken rule an entry the constructor built on another commission than the grant's, by another actor or at another time.

The handler answers `Handled { answer }`; the gate refuses an answer whose id isn't the grant's commission (or the minted id), and the answer leaves the write as `ArmAnswer` in `WriteResult`. A typed call builds its values from that answer plus the name and level the gate wrote; no node is read back.

No lint silencer in any production file of the use-case layer (`application/src`, the crate root and every module file included): no `allow` or `expect` of `dead_code`, `unused`, `unused_variables`, `unreachable_code` or `warnings`, outer, inner, under `cfg_attr`, in bodies and macro bodies, so none sits in the den, on a module above it, or in an act however its handler is written. An item no real act reaches is removed, never silenced; `tests/write_gate_seams.rs` (`no_production_source_holds_a_lint_silencer`) holds it.
An existing commission's grant is bound to the node its locked standing read answered: the walk refuses a top row that isn't that node as a store failure, so a write lands only on the bound node.

fs.name: access.rs
fs.role: den's access check: may this viewer open the node a read that bypasses the Den serves, named by typed ids; Atta's own resolve, open on exactly its real path, else the one not-found; the check keeps the plain walk and never tells equal names apart, pinned by access/tests.rs. Commission's download and changelog read call it; identity's reads (the viewer's own root, an Account) are next

fs.name: act.rs
fs.role: DenAct, the enum of every act the write carries (the commission's CommissionAct), its ActSpec (word, type, Anchor, the needed CommissionRole read from its capability's role, None for a create, and ActShape: Create or Rename), BornEntry (a fixed word as key and name, a type, a picked level), EntryConstructor (a gated kind's domain constructor: commission, actor, time in, NewChangelogEntry out), EntryRule (Always a constructor, or OnChange: one entry only when the act changed its node), Handled (the handler's answer: the Commission its lent view read), ArmAnswer (that answer as it leaves the write, with a hand-written Debug that prints the id, never the owner's DID) and HandlerError (a store failure under the handler)

fs.name: admission.rs
fs.role: the admit table: live, archived and deactivated nodes by access, reach and include_deleted

fs.name: authority.rs
fs.role: who may write where: `admit`, the pool's verdict before any unit opens (a top-level anchor by rule, only a create, only /commission; a commission by commission::den::pool_verdict), and `grant`, made inside the unit from standing_for_update under the same rules; a thing anchor whose act needs no role fails closed as WrongGrant on both; Grant (private fields, no Clone/Default, one private constructor plus a cfg(test) for_test) over GrantKind (Existing commission+role+level bound to the node the locked read answered, or Create under an id minted here by CommissionId::mint, v7, never the act's); cfg(test) MINT_AS plants the next minted id; authority/tests.rs: on the pool and in the unit, the fail-closed rule, a rename with a top-level anchor refused, a place or top level with no arm the one not-found

fs.name: context.rs
fs.role: DenContext: the ports, the session viewer and the read's RootNaming (look up, or the cache only) every arm receives

fs.name: den_type.rs
fs.role: DenType, its 21 wire words, and the kind and content-not-shown tables; commission.brief and commission.participants are files whose content isn't shown, and unserved: no arm projects them, so nothing lists them

fs.name: gate.rs
fs.role: DenWriteHost, the write's atta::Host (serves no read, kind from type_kind, the unit in a Mutex read through get_mut, apply refuses another viewer) and the gate it runs once per act: grant kind, D-1 (nothing wider than Private until 0.6), the node rows walked from the grant's commission, its top row refused unless it is the node the grant is bound to, and written under the one `nodes()` binding (SegmentTaken recognised once; a rename to the stored name writes nothing; Atta's change shape a broken rule; Written carries the node acted on or made and whether a row changed), the act lent by `lend` (one `lend_as` per leaf act: create, rename) to its Handler, then the act's entry built here by its Handler's ENTRY rule's domain constructor as the rule says of what changed (on the grant's commission, by its actor, at now; built_entry refuses an entry the constructor built anywhere else as a broken rule); RoleTable (NEEDS, granted, commission) for AsParticipant, AsOwner and Creator, `needs::<H>()` reading an act's role from its marker, `issue` (the one gate_issued call), `lend_as::<H>` (the one issue call: a Lent view over the commission repo, the capability, the gate's node, the grant's actor and now; a tripped Latch fails the act whatever the handler answered; an answer naming another commission than the grant's is a broken rule); Lent's surface is create (a creator's only) and lent (every role), each through the latch; DenApplied carries the ArmAnswer, its Debug printing no name and no DID; refusals ride inside Applied, store failures as HostError; gate/tests.rs (with the gate/tests/spy.rs double over a real unit, which can redirect or fail commission reads and refuse appends): the role table, another viewer, a create through the write host, the latch on each adapter (a test-only swallowing creator lent through lend_as), a failed handler read, the answer check, the gate's node, owner and time, one created entry, the create's and the rename's entries with an empty payload and no note on each adapter, an entry built off the grant's commission, actor or time a broken rule, one unit, no node read after a create's or a rename's writes on PostgreSQL

fs.name: host.rs
fs.role: DenHost, the one atta::Host for reads: the request record, the viewer check, the dispatch to each team's arm; its record answers each open node's soft-deleted word and thing; `found` names a node through names::display_name; `type_kind` is the one kind table every den host answers from (a type key the Den doesn't know is a file); `for_check` builds den's access check's host, whose reads name the viewer's root from the cache only; its apply is Atta's refusing default (host/tests.rs pins it)

fs.name: kind.rs
fs.role: NodeKind: directory, file, symlink

fs.name: level.rs
fs.role: atta_level, the one map from kernel's Level to Atta's, run in DenHost::found and the write's builder; den_level maps Atta's answer back for the output and the gate's rows

fs.name: name.rs
fs.role: DenName (From kernel's NodeName) and DenNameError: the Den's name rule, the write-side check every naming write calls and the re-check every read makes of the names Atta answers with; showable_refusal names kernel's ShowableName refusals (Account founding) in the same DenNameError

fs.name: name_ordinal.rs
fs.role: NameOrdinal and NameOrdinalError: the application's own number that tells equal names apart, over Atta's, 2 or more (TryFrom<u32>, From into u32)

fs.name: names.rs
fs.role: the fixed folder and entry words (a commission's six entries among them: attachments, products, slots, changelog, participants, brief), the id and DID keys (id_segment takes only the typed UUID ids, through the den trait UuidKey), the stored-text name with its `Unnamed` fallback, and display_name, the one place a name enters Atta (DisplayName::host_checked, banned everywhere else by application/clippy.toml, its #[expect] failing the gate if the ban stops matching)

fs.name: node.rs
fs.role: the `node` Query: a Den path below the viewer's root; after the plain walk succeeds, Atta's tell_apart numbers the node and its crumbs; node/tests.rs: per-viewer numbering, the archived twin, nothing stored

fs.name: output.rs
fs.role: the Queries' output values: DenNode, DenAccess (an open node's thing among its facts), DenCrumb (with its type), each DenNode and DenCrumb with its name_ordinal, DenListing, DenContent

fs.name: page_token.rs
fs.role: PageToken, the application's own token over Atta's, with FromStr/Display

fs.name: place.rs
fs.role: Place, Parent, TopLevel, Place::is_child_of, Place::thing (an Account's or a commission's directory names its id; every other place none), Node (an arm's answer), DenMount and the STANDING lift

fs.name: post.rs
fs.role: den's arm for /post/<did>: the empty posts stub, named `posts`, Public, the same for every DID; it takes no ports, so it reads no store and calls no host; nothing below it

fs.name: read.rs
fs.role: the Queries' shared read: path parsing, the viewer's root, the Reader over any atta::Host plus a RecordLookup (each open node's soft-deleted word and thing, in one lookup), Atta's answers into output values; each node's and crumb's name is re-checked by the Den's name rule on its way out, a refusal a store error whose text carries no name (read/proptests.rs walks stored text in through stored_name and out again); a crumb carries its entry's type, an unknown one a store error; Reader::tell_apart numbers a walked node and its crumbs, and every node and crumb carries Atta's number as its name_ordinal

fs.name: root.rs
fs.role: the `root` Query: the viewer's own root and its listing

fs.name: segment.rs
fs.role: DenSegment: one Den path piece in an answer

fs.name: soft_delete.rs
fs.role: SoftDelete: archived, deactivated

fs.name: state.rs
fs.role: NodeState: live, archived, deactivated (with whether the viewer is the Owner)

fs.name: test_acts.rs
fs.role: cfg(test) only: the real create and rename acts as DenAct (create_act, rename_act), a commission's real path, and Atta's acts built by hand around a real act's body (a rename onto any type at any path, a create keyed by any id at any picked level) for the tests that drive the write host below the den's builder

fs.name: thing.rs
fs.role: DenThing: the Account or commission an open node stands for, by its id

fs.name: write.rs
fs.role: the `write` use case (pub(crate), #[lazy_unit]): admit on the pool, open the unit, grant from the locked standing, the one builder of Atta's act (paths from the grant's typed ids, an existing node's level from the locked read, a create's key from the minted id, each entry named by its word), Writer::act through DenWriteHost; Command, WriteResult (the thing, the name, the level and the handler's ArmAnswer; a hand-written Debug with no name and no DID), DenWriteError (NotFound, Forbidden, Refused(RefusalClass), Store) and RefusalClass; write/tests.rs proves each rule on the real create and rename acts on memory, and the marked ones on PostgreSQL (the bound node, the no-op rename, one renamed entry, the grant binding the write); write/log_tests.rs: four writes at trace on PostgreSQL log no identity at info, no name, no store detail; a create whose commission insert PostgreSQL refuses on its owner key, with a DETAIL naming the DID, is latched: the error keeps the DETAIL as its source, and no line at any level carries the DETAIL or a DID

notes: The identity arms (user, Account, Character) answer from slice 9; the commission arms from slice 10; the `/post/<did>` stub from slice 16, so a user's `posts` mount opens Public, its content not shown and its listing empty, and every path below it is the one not-found. The commission arms and the stub are also tested through the host from their real paths (`test_world::read`).

A folder's contents belong to the arm that owns its entries: a user's `commissions` folder and an Account's `commissions` folder are `CommissionPlace`s, and an Account's `workflows` folder is a `WorkflowPlace`, though identity answers each folder node as a child of its user or Account.
